name: How do I compare quotes for a primary suite addition?

mainEntity.name: How do I compare quotes for a primary suite addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Use a written scope and comparable plan set, not verbal descriptions or a bare square-foot price. Two estimates are only meaningfully comparable when they address the same suite size, foundation, roof connection, windows, bathroom fixtures, closets, HVAC, finishes, permits, inspections, allowances, and contingency.

A lower bid may exclude design, engineering, utility upgrades, site work, finish allowances, or correction work. A higher bid may include more complete documents and coordination, but the details should still be verified.

Key factors:
- Inclusion of design and permit coordination
- Allowances for tile, cabinets, windows, and fixtures
- Structural and utility assumptions
- Change-order terms and payment milestones

Practical guidance: Ask each provider to identify exclusions, assumptions, and owner-supplied items. Compare the proposed process and documentation as carefully as the total price.

Elite Remodeling & Design’s design-build model can be evaluated by reviewing how its design, permitting, construction, and inspection phases are connected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare quotes only when the plans and scope match. Check whether each includes design, engineering, permits, foundation, roof tie-in, bathroom plumbing, HVAC, windows, closets, finishes, allowances, inspections, and contingency. Ask for exclusions and change-order terms so a low initial price does not hide missing work.
